brute_force_nested.label: Nested Loop (Brute Force)
brute_force_nested.tier1: Your solution uses nested loops. Think about what work the inner loop is doing — is it scanning for something that could be looked up instantly?
brute_force_nested.tier2: Consider whether a hash map or set could replace the inner loop. If you are checking 'is X in this collection?', a set answers that in O(1) instead of O(n).

hash_optimization.label: Hash Map / Set Approach
hash_optimization.tier1: You are using a hash structure — that's the right direction. Check whether you are storing the right keys and looking up the right complements.
hash_optimization.tier2: Make sure you handle the case where a value maps to itself. Are you checking the complement before or after inserting the current element?

pointer_convergence.label: Two-Pointer / Convergence
pointer_convergence.tier1: Your pointers are moving — but are they moving in the right direction? Think about what condition should make each pointer advance.
pointer_convergence.tier2: With sorted input, two pointers from opposite ends can skip large sections. If the sum is too large, which pointer should move? If too small?

stack_pattern.label: Stack-Based Approach
stack_pattern.tier1: You are using a stack — good instinct. Consider what should happen when you pop: does the popped item match what you expect?
stack_pattern.tier2: Think about edge cases: what if the stack is empty when you try to pop? What if there are items left on the stack at the end?

binary_search.label: Binary Search
binary_search.tier1: You are halving the search space — make sure your boundary updates don't skip the target or loop forever.
binary_search.tier2: Check your mid calculation and boundary updates. After comparing nums[mid] with target, should you set left = mid + 1 or left = mid? An off-by-one here causes infinite loops or missed targets.

single_pass.label: Single Pass
single_pass.tier1: Your approach uses a single loop — think about whether you are tracking all the state you need as you go.
single_pass.tier2: A single-pass solution often needs an accumulator or auxiliary variable. Are you updating it at the right point in the loop — before or after the check?

recursive.label: Recursive Approach
recursive.tier1: You are using recursion. Make sure your base case covers all termination conditions and that each recursive call makes progress toward the base case.
recursive.tier2: Check whether your recursive calls are exploring too many branches. Could memoization or an iterative approach reduce repeated work?

linear_search_in_loop.label: Linear Search Inside Loop
linear_search_in_loop.tier1: You are using 'in' to search a list inside a loop. Each 'in' check scans the entire list, turning your O(n) loop into O(n²).
linear_search_in_loop.tier2: Convert the list to a set before the loop. Set lookups are O(1) on average, which brings the total back down to O(n).

unknown.label: General Guidance
unknown.tier1: Start by identifying the core operation: are you searching, sorting, or transforming? Pick the data structure that makes that operation cheap.
unknown.tier2: Break the problem into smaller steps. What must be true before you can compute the answer? Can you precompute any of those conditions?
